title: Hydrodynamic and Hydroacoustic Performance Analysis of a Bionic Rim-Driven Thruster
content: Rim-driven thrusters (RDTs) are emerging as next-generation marine electric propulsion systems, offering advantages such as flexibility, environmental friendliness, high efficiency, and the elimination of cooling and lubrication systems. Nevertheless, existing RDTs face persistent challenges including limited hydrodynamic efficiency and noise problems. To address these limitations, this study introduces a passive flow control strategy inspired by the tubercles on humpback whale flippers. Bionic protuberances are applied to the blades’ leading and trailing edges, and their effects on hydrodynamic performance and flow-induced noise are systematically investigated. Results indicate that certain tubercles on the blades enhance efficiency and improve noise performance in the mid-to-low frequency range. Within the optimal trailing edge tubercle series, smaller wavelengths combined with larger amplitudes yield a higher efficiency, with the best configuration achieving a 2.1% improvement over the baseline under design conditions. This gain is attributed to an increased pressure differential across the blade and reduced shear stress, which together augment thrust while lowering torque. For noise performance improvement, blade-mounted tubercles effectively break down large-scale vortices and accelerate wake dissipation, resulting in a low-frequency noise reduction of up to 5-10 dB in the optimal design.
